body.statement: For fixed \(k,d_x,d_z\) and a population law \(P\), write \(M_{ZX\mid t}(P):=E_P[ZX^\top\mid T=t]\), \(M_{\mathrm{stack}}(P):=[M_{ZX\mid 0}(P)^\top,M_{ZX\mid 1}(P)^\top]^\top\), and let \(V_k(P)\) be an orthonormal basis for the population \(k\)-dimensional right singular subspace of \(M_{\mathrm{stack}}(P)\).  VMW Assumption 4 is the law-level requirement that there exist finite positive constants \(L_X,L_{ZX},L_{ZXY}\) for which \(\lVert X\rVert_2\le L_X\), \(\lVert ZX^\top\rVert_2\le L_{ZX}\), and \(\lVert YZX^\top\rVert_2\le L_{ZXY}\) almost surely under \(P\), while \(\pi(P):=\min_{t\in\{0,1\}}P(T=t)>0\) and \(\sigma(P):=\min\{\sigma_k(M_{\mathrm{stack}}(P)),\min_{t\in\{0,1\}}\sigma_k(M_{ZX\mid t}(P)V_k(P))\}>0\).  It subsequently defines \(M_X,M_Y,\kappa_B,\Gamma_X,\Gamma_Y\), and \(\kappa_{ZX}^{\star}\) as fixed derived conditioning quantities, not as additional conjunctive assumptions.  VMW Theorem 7.2 operates under the standing Assumption 1 conditions \(Z\perp(X,Y)\mid(T,U)\), \(X\perp(Y,T)\mid U\), causal consistency \(Y=Y(T)\), and latent ignorability \(Y(t)\perp T\mid U\), together with the anchor normalization \(X_1=1\) almost surely.  It additionally assumes Assumption 2, strict latent positivity, Assumption 4, and spectral separation, where spectral separation means \(\tau(u)\ne\tau(v)\) for distinct \(u,v\in\{1,\ldots,k\}\) and is vacuous for \(k=1\).  Together with its stated \(n,\eta\)-dependent sample-size and radius conditions, the theorem gives simultaneous high-probability finite-sample recovery of the treatment effects, the anchor-normalized feature matrix, and the simplex-projected mixture weights.  Consequently, when \(k\ge2\), a treatment-effect collision lies outside the separated recovery regime of VMW Theorem 7.2.

source.verbatim_statement: The standing model assumes \(Z\perp\!\!\!\perp(X,Y)\mid(T,U)\), \(X\perp\!\!\!\perp(Y,T)\mid U\), causal consistency \(Y=Y(T)\), latent ignorability, and the anchor normalization \(X_1=1\).  For fixed \(k,d_x,d_z\), Assumption 4 requires finite \(L_X,L_{ZX},L_{ZXY}>0\) with \(\lVert X\rVert_2\le L_X\), \(\lVert ZX^\top\rVert_2\le L_{ZX}\), and \(\lVert YZX^\top\rVert_2\le L_{ZXY}\) almost surely; it requires \(\pi:=\min_{t\in\{0,1\}}\Pr(T=t)>0\) and, for the population right singular basis \(V_k\) of \(M_{\mathrm{stack}}\), \(\sigma:=\min\{\sigma_k(M_{\mathrm{stack}}),\min_{t\in\{0,1\}}\sigma_k(M_{ZX\mid t}V_k)\}>0\).  The displayed \(M_X,M_Y,\kappa_B,\Gamma_X,\Gamma_Y\), and \(\kappa_{ZX}^{\star}\) are then defined as fixed population conditioning quantities.  Assumption 3 requires \(\tau(u)\ne\tau(v)\) for every \(u\ne v\).  Within the standing qualitative model and anchor normalization, Theorem 7.2 assumes Assumption 2, strict latent positivity, Assumption 4, and spectral separation, takes the latter as vacuous when \(k=1\), imposes its displayed \(n,\eta\)-dependent radius conditions, and concludes simultaneous finite-sample bounds for the effects, anchor-normalized feature matrix, and simplex-projected mixture proportions.
